texts: On bypass with a single femoral venous cannula, poor drainage with a rising central venous pressure and a distended right heart during left atrial retraction is best fixed by adding a second venous cannula in the superior vena cava.
Retracting the left atrium can kink or compress the venous pathway, so blood from the upper body pools in the superior vena cava and the right atrium.
A separate SVC cannula drains the upper body directly and decompresses the heart and the venous outflow of the brain.
Pulling the femoral cannula back or upsizing it does not drain blood trapped above the retractor, and moving the arterial cannula does nothing for venous drainage.
In the picture, the hook pinches the pipe, so Franky pushes a second cannon into the chimney and the trapped blue water drains again.
Memory hook: one cannon from below, one more from above.
